title: Hierarchical chat-command permissions with follower and subscriber roles

functional.description: Replace editable explicit role allowlists with one minimum access level per configurable command. Selecting a level grants access to that level and every higher level in the product hierarchy.
functional.rationale: The owner requested inherited group permissions so commands can be granted to subscribers and above.

functional.description: Use the product policy order everyone < follower < subscriber < VIP < moderator < streamer. Treat this as an application authorization order, not as a Twitch-defined hierarchy. A message may prove multiple roles; effective access is its highest currently verified role.
functional.rationale: The owner approved followers below subscribers; higher groups inherit lower-level command access.

functional.description: Recognize the streamer only by configured broadcaster user ID; recognize moderator, VIP, and subscriber from trusted badges on the current target-channel chat message; recognize follower through a current Helix lookup by Twitch user ID.
functional.rationale: Chat text, login names, mentions, stale badges, and Shared Chat source-channel roles are not authorization evidence.

functional.description: Add follower-based command access using GET /helix/channels/followers with broadcaster_id and user_id. Request moderator:read:followers only when the streamer enables a follower threshold; otherwise preserve the existing three OAuth scopes.
functional.rationale: The owner explicitly approved a follower role and its additional scope; least privilege requires requesting the extra scope only when used.

functional.description: Before treating an empty follower result as not-following, confirm the current broadcaster token is valid, belongs to the configured client/broadcaster, and includes moderator:read:followers. Missing scope, API failure, timeout, 429, 5xx, or malformed response produces an unknown role and fails closed for follower-gated actions.
functional.rationale: Twitch documents that an empty response can also mean missing scope or authorization; unknown must not become a grant or a false definitive denial.

functional.description: Keep all queue-management commands fixed to streamer and authorized target-channel moderators. Keep !conta <nome> and !conta reset streamer-only. Keep !queue ping streamer/moderator-only. The panel/API cannot broaden these fixed rules.
functional.rationale: These are explicit product-owner permission boundaries; account mutation is stricter than the general queue-management rule.

functional.description: Keep the global VIP-management toggle as a hard gate on VIP-derived access. A user with an independent higher trusted role still qualifies through that role; a VIP badge alone does not qualify while the toggle is disabled.
functional.rationale: Preserve the existing safety toggle while making role inheritance deterministic.

functional.description: Render the configured minimum level and effective inherited audience in the protected command catalog; show fixed streamer/moderator rules as locked. Render chat help using the same policy resolver and the sender's verified effective role; keep each response within Twitch's 500-character product limit.
functional.rationale: Panel, help, and authorization must describe the same actual rule.

functional.description: Preserve existing saved array allowlists exactly during upgrade. Store them as legacy-exact policies until the streamer explicitly selects and saves a hierarchical minimum level for that command; show the current effective audience and a review state before conversion.
functional.rationale: A single threshold cannot represent every former OR allowlist. Automatic conversion could silently broaden or revoke access.

functional.description: When a streamer selects a follower minimum without the required scope, initiate a session-bound OAuth authorization for the additional scope. Do not save the policy until the returned token is validated for the same client/broadcaster and the scope is confirmed. If consent fails or is declined, retain the previous token and policy.
functional.rationale: The scope is optional and should be requested only for the feature that needs it; failed consent must not disrupt an existing integration.

functional.description: Use Twitch user IDs for follower checks; do not persist follower lists, follower membership, badge snapshots, or role assignments. Do not use channel.follow notifications as current-membership proof because they only report new follows.
functional.rationale: Avoid stale authorization and minimize stored personal data.

functional.description: Retain the current command roots localized by product locale (!fila, !queue, !cola) and do not create separate authorization roles for translated labels. The distinct Twitch criteria are subscriber badge and follower relationship; localize their labels by locale.
functional.rationale: FND-8 owns product localization; localized names must not create duplicate security identities.

nonFunctional.description: All authorization decisions fail closed on missing identity, untrusted source channel, unavailable follower verification, unknown policy schema, missing scope, or malformed stored policy.
nonFunctional.metric: No protected operation, point action, account lookup, queue lookup, or mutation occurs after an unresolved/denied authorization decision.

nonFunctional.description: Follower verification uses only broadcaster ID and current event user ID; do not store raw Helix responses, user lists, follower timestamps, or role snapshots.
nonFunctional.metric: Tests and audit projections show no follower membership or raw Twitch response persistence/logging.

nonFunctional.description: A failure to verify follower status affects only commands whose configured minimum requires follower proof; other authenticated Twitch/chat behavior and lower-threshold commands remain available.
nonFunctional.metric: Failure injection demonstrates unrelated commands continue while follower-gated mutation remains unexecuted.

nonFunctional.description: The protected panel explains the minimum threshold, inherited groups, VIP toggle, extra Twitch consent, and legacy exact policies before save.
nonFunctional.metric: A streamer can identify the effective allowed audience and any needed authorization before committing a policy change.

nonFunctional.description: Follower lookup occurs only after parsing a recognized command whose authorization/help projection needs follower status; known higher roles bypass the lookup. Concurrent same-user checks may share an in-flight request but must not reuse a stale completed result.
nonFunctional.metric: Tests prove no follower API request for unrelated messages, everyone-level commands, known qualifying subscriber/moderator/streamer, or commands already denied by a higher threshold.

constraints.description: Remain JavaScript ESM, Fastify, vanilla frontend, Prisma/PostgreSQL, and existing Twurple packages at the pinned repository version; no new service or dependency is required.
constraints.impact: Use the canonical command registry, existing protected routes, existing OAuth session/state, Twitch adapter, and JSON setting persistence.

constraints.description: The existing OAuth scopes remain channel:manage:redemptions, user:read:chat, and user:write:chat. moderator:read:followers is optional and required only for follower-level policy.
constraints.impact: Do not add scopes for unrelated channel features; optional scope consent must preserve the current valid credential if it fails.

constraints.description: The policy ladder everyone < follower < subscriber < VIP < moderator < streamer is an application-defined grant hierarchy, not a claim that Twitch defines these roles as mutually exclusive ranks.
constraints.impact: Twitch evidence may overlap. Effective role is the highest trusted applicable claim under current toggle and channel identity.

constraints.description: Queue management commands remain streamer/moderator-only; account label set/reset remain streamer-only; global ping remains streamer/moderator-only; streamer identity is never editable.
constraints.impact: These registry definitions are immutable and API payloads cannot relax them.

constraints.description: Existing version-1 explicit allowlist JSON can represent non-contiguous audiences that a minimum-role policy cannot exactly represent.
constraints.impact: Read as legacy-exact and retain its effective decision until the streamer explicitly converts the command; never automatically broaden or narrow it.

constraints.description: The app is a single-channel local installation and authenticates as the broadcaster. Shared Chat from another source channel remains rejected for authorization and command processing.
constraints.impact: Follower checks use the configured broadcaster ID and the current chat event's Twitch user ID only.

assumptions.description: For Portuguese UI, `subscriber` is labeled `Inscritos`, `follower` is labeled `Seguidores`, and the English UI labels these `Subscribers` and `Followers`; Spanish labels use the corresponding localized forms.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: The role criteria stay distinct, but displayed labels would need owner correction before UX implementation.

assumptions.description: The installed `@twurple/api`, `@twurple/auth`, and `@twurple/eventsub-ws` versions are all 8.2.0; the API adapter can call `api.channels.getChannelFollowers(broadcasterId, userId)` and the auth provider exposes current token scopes.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Revalidate package declarations before implementation if dependency versions change.

acceptanceCriteria.given: A streamer configures a mutable command threshold
acceptanceCriteria.when: the minimum is everyone, follower, subscriber, VIP, or moderator
acceptanceCriteria.then: the stored policy is a single supported threshold and every higher verified role inherits access; the broadcaster retains identity-based access to configurable commands and identity is never supplied by the client.

acceptanceCriteria.given: A message carries overlapping trusted role evidence
acceptanceCriteria.then: the highest verified role is used; VIP evidence is ignored when the existing VIP toggle is off, while independent subscriber/moderator/broadcaster evidence remains effective.

acceptanceCriteria.given: The command is queue management, account mutation, or ping
acceptanceCriteria.when: a viewer changes panel policy or sends the command
acceptanceCriteria.then: the fixed role boundary applies regardless of stored input; account mutations are broadcaster-only.

acceptanceCriteria.given: A chat event is from the configured channel
acceptanceCriteria.then: only `badges` on that current event and exact broadcaster user ID count; no old message, login, display name, body field, or source-channel badge is reused.

acceptanceCriteria.given: A message has a foreign Shared Chat source or wrong channel
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is rejected before lookups, follower calls, queue effects, account effects, chat replies, or financial operations.

acceptanceCriteria.given: A command/help projection requires follower status and the user has no already-qualifying higher role
acceptanceCriteria.then: it calls the documented user-filtered Helix endpoint with broadcaster/user IDs and uses only a successful, scope-authorized, identity-matched result.

acceptanceCriteria.given: Follower status is unavailable, missing scope, expired/revoked auth, malformed, rate limited, timed out, or 5xx
acceptanceCriteria.then: the result is unknown/denied, no command mutation or outbox intent occurs, safe localized feedback is used, and unrelated lower-level commands continue.

acceptanceCriteria.given: The streamer selects a follower threshold without the optional scope
acceptanceCriteria.then: the session-bound OAuth request asks only for the existing required scopes plus `moderator:read:followers`; persist the new grant/policy only after callback state, client, broadcaster, token, and actual scope validation succeed.

acceptanceCriteria.given: The Twitch API returns empty follower data
acceptanceCriteria.then: the app distinguishes a confirmed non-follower from missing scope/authorization using the current token scope state; empty data alone never grants access.

acceptanceCriteria.given: A panel or chat request targets an immutable role rule
acceptanceCriteria.then: the immutable audience is enforced and unauthorized requests cause no downstream effect.

acceptanceCriteria.given: The streamer opens the command catalog
acceptanceCriteria.then: minimum group, inherited audience, locked role, follower-scope readiness, and localized names are derived from the same canonical registry/resolver used in chat.

acceptanceCriteria.given: A viewer requests global or queue-specific command help
acceptanceCriteria.then: only commands they can currently use are listed, follower status is checked only if needed, unavailable follower status never reveals follower-gated commands, and output stays under 500 characters.

acceptanceCriteria.given: Version-1 policy JSON contains explicit allowlists
acceptanceCriteria.then: each list remains legacy-exact in effective authorization and the schema does not rewrite the saved record or widen/narrow access on startup.

acceptanceCriteria.given: A streamer edits a legacy-exact command
acceptanceCriteria.when: the UI shows old and proposed effective access and the streamer confirms a new threshold
acceptanceCriteria.then: only that command converts to inherited policy; other legacy settings remain unchanged; audit records actor, command ID, before/after policy mode and version without role lookup payloads.

acceptanceCriteria.given: Follower-scope reauthorization is declined, invalid, mismatched, or missing the granted scope
acceptanceCriteria.then: the previous valid credentials and command policy remain intact and the UI explains the missing permission without showing secrets or raw errors.

acceptanceCriteria.given: Follower checks are made across commands and restarts
acceptanceCriteria.when: the database, audit, logs, and cache are inspected
acceptanceCriteria.then: no follower list, follower membership, stale role snapshot, or raw Helix response was persisted; only in-flight request deduplication may share work.

acceptanceCriteria.given: The selected product locale is English, pt-BR, or Spanish
acceptanceCriteria.when: command syntax and role labels are rendered
acceptanceCriteria.then: command roots and group labels follow FND-8 catalogs while role IDs and authorization semantics remain language-neutral.

ownerDecisions: Inherited group semantics are approved; follower is a distinct group below subscriber.
The optional Twitch scope moderator:read:followers is approved when follower-based access is enabled.
The conditional beta-stage promotion is authorized only after OPS-7, OPS-8, FND-9, and DOC-2 are complete; no stage change is authorized before then.
